text.id: Dicatat sebagai patianac oleh Juan de Plasencia pada 1589.
text.en: Recorded as the patianac by Juan de Plasencia in 1589.

cultural_context.id: Menurut sebuah artikel tentang makhluk ini, kisah-kisah tiyanak merekam kenyataan sosial seputar kelahiran dan masa kanak-kanak: kehamilan dan persalinan berbahaya, kematian bayi lazim, dan tangisan tak dikenal menuntut tanggapan moral, sehingga belas kasih menjadi perangkapnya.
cultural_context.en: According to an article on the creature, tiyanak stories preserve the social realities of birth and childhood: pregnancy and labour were dangerous, infant mortality was common and an unexplained cry demanded a moral response.

who.id: Makhluk pengisap darah yang menyamar sebagai bayi.
who.en: A vampiric creature that disguises itself as a baby.

role.id: Pemikat dan penyesat pejalan di hutan.
role.en: A lurer and misleader of travellers in the jungle.

famous_for.en: The baby's cry that lures victims.

did_you_know.id: Catatan tertua, dari 1589, tentang patianac tidak menggambarkan bayi pemikat, melainkan perempuan dan anak yang mati saat melahirkan dan terdengar meratap pada malam hari.
did_you_know.en: The oldest record, from 1589, of the patianac does not describe a baby lure but a woman and child who died in childbirth and were heard lamenting at night.

description.id: Menjelma bayi dan kembali ke wujud aslinya saat diangkat; meniru tangisan bayi untuk memikat korban; dalam satu catatan tubuh bayi berubah menjadi kakek kecil, dan dalam legenda Mindoro berubah menjadi burung hitam.
description.en: Takes a baby's form and reverts to its true form when picked up; imitates an infant's cries to lure victims; in one account a baby's body turns into a small old man, and in a Mindoro legend it turns into a black bird.

description.id: Dalam beberapa cerita tiyanak terlihat terbang di hutan atau terbang pergi sesudah menyerang korbannya.
description.en: In some stories the tiyanak is seen flying through the forest or flying away after attacking its victim.

description.id: Makhluk semacam ini dikatakan dapat menjadi terlihat atau tak terlihat.
description.en: Such beings were said to become visible or invisible.

description.id: Membalik pakaian mematahkan pesona atau daya tipunya.
description.en: Turning clothes inside out breaks its enchantment or power of deception.

description.id: Suara keras seperti perayaan Tahun Baru dipercaya mengusirnya, dan dalam satu kisah warga memukul kaleng timah agar makhluk-makhluk itu melepaskan korban.
description.en: Loud noises such as a New Year's celebration are believed to drive it away, and in one story villagers struck tin cans so the beings would release a victim.

description.id: Menurut Jose A. Samson, kepercayaan umum albularyo di pedesaan Luzon adalah memainkan gitar untuk menangkalnya.
description.en: According to Jose A. Samson, a common belief among albularyos in rural Luzon is to play the guitar to ward it off.

description.id: Orang kecil berkulit cokelat kacang yang melayang di udara; dalam kisah Kapampangan sekelompok dari mereka muncul di Gunung Arayat.
description.en: Small nut-brown people floating in the air; in the Kapampangan story a crowd of them appeared on Mount Arayat.

description.id: Dalam legenda dari pulau Mindoro tiyanak berubah menjadi burung hitam sebelum terbang pergi.
description.en: In a legend from the island of Mindoro the tiyanak turns into a black bird before flying away.

description.id: Digambarkan sebagai bayi biasa yang tersesat di alam liar.
description.en: Described as regular babies who were lost in the wild.

description.id: Arwah anak yang ibunya meninggal sebelum melahirkan.
description.en: The spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth.

role.id: Bayi penemuan yang menggigit dan lalu terbang pergi.
role.en: A foundling infant that bites and then flies away.

summary.id: Sepasang suami istri menemukan bayi di hutan dan membawanya; bayi itu menempel pada dada sang istri dan menggigitnya, sang istri ditemukan mati, dan bayi itu terlihat terbang pergi di antara pepohonan.
summary.en: A couple find an infant in the forest and carry it with them; it fastens onto the wife's breast and bites her, she is found dead, and the infant is seen flying away among the trees.

role.id: Bayi menyerupai anak yang telah dikubur.
role.en: An infant resembling the buried child.

summary.id: Seorang bayi menyusu tanpa henti pada seorang ibu sampai ibu itu meninggal; sesudahnya bayi itu berubah menjadi burung hitam dan terbang dari rumah.
summary.en: An infant feeds without stopping at a mother's breast until she dies, after which it changes into a black bird and flies from the house.

role.id: Anak penggoda yang membawa Bata pergi.
role.en: A child who leads Bata away.

summary.id: Kisah ini ditutup dengan penjelasan bahwa tianac adalah anak yang meninggal tanpa dibaptis, yang berkeliaran di tempat sunyi dan menyesatkan anak muda; membalik pakaian disebut sebagai penangkalnya.
summary.en: The tale ends by identifying the tianac as a child who died unbaptized, said to roam lonely places and mislead the young; turning one's clothing inside out is named as the way to break its deception.

title.en: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac (Kapampangan)

role.id: Kerumunan makhluk kecil yang menyesatkan seorang lelaki di gunung.
role.en: A crowd of small beings that mislead a man on a mountain.

summary.id: Vicente bertemu banyak tianac di Gunung Arayat; ia lenyapkan mereka dengan membalik pakaiannya, dan baru kemudian mengetahui bahwa hari sudah Senin padahal ia mengira hanya terlambat satu jam.
summary.en: Vicente meets many tianac on Mount Arayat; he makes them vanish by turning his clothes inside out and only afterwards learns that it is Monday although he believed he was merely an hour late.

role.id: Makhluk yang diduga membawa pergi seorang penjaga kolam.
role.en: Beings suspected of taking away a fishpond watchman.

summary.id: Warga kampung menduga tianak membawa seorang penjaga kolam ikan yang tua dan mencarinya sambil memukul kaleng timah terus-menerus agar makhluk-makhluk itu melepaskannya.
summary.en: Villagers suspect the tianak have taken an elderly fishpond watchman and search for him while striking tin cans continuously so the beings will release him.

description.id: Tempat Vicente bertemu banyak tianac dalam kisah Kapampangan.
description.en: Where Vicente encounters many tianac in the Kapampangan story.

description.id: Dalam legenda dari pulau ini tiyanak berubah menjadi burung hitam.
description.en: In a legend from this island the tiyanak turns into a black bird.

description.id: Fr. Juan de Plasencia mencatat kepercayaan tentang patianac di kalangan orang Tagalog.
description.en: Fr. Juan de Plasencia records belief in the patianac among the Tagalogs.

description.id: Fr. Francisco de San Antonio mencatat para pria yang menanggalkan pakaian saat persalinan untuk menjauhkan patianac.
description.en: Fr. Francisco de San Antonio records men undressing during childbirth to keep the patianac away.

description.id: Martinez de Zuniga mencatat bahwa suami mengayunkan pedang untuk melawan patianac sampai istrinya bersalin.
description.en: Martinez de Zuniga records the husband flourishing a sword against the patianac until his wife was delivered.

note.id: Makhluk gaib serupa dalam cerita rakyat Melayu, yang berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal sebelum melahirkan.
note.en: A similar supernatural creature in Malay folklore, which was a woman who died before giving birth.

description.id: Tiyanak menjadi subjek banyak film Filipina, di antaranya Tianak (1953) dan Tiyanak (1988).
description.en: The tiyanak is the subject of many Philippine films, among them Tianak (1953) and Tiyanak (1988).

traditional.id: Catatan tertua tentang patianac menyangkut perempuan dan anak yang mati saat melahirkan, bukan bayi pemikat.
traditional.en: The oldest record of the patianac concerns a woman and child who died in childbirth, not a baby lure.

modern.id: Penulis dan seniman modern menafsirkan ulang tiyanak; satu penafsiran membacanya sebagai bayi yang berusaha memahami dunia kejam ciptaan orang dewasa.
modern.en: Modern writers and artists reinterpret the tiyanak; one reading approaches it as a newborn trying to understand a violent world created by adults.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa kepercayaan tentang tiyanak berubah setelah datangnya agama Katolik?
learning_questions.en: Why did beliefs about the tiyanak change after Catholicism arrived?

learning_questions.id: Mengapa tangisan bayi menjadi perangkap yang efektif dalam cerita ini?
learning_questions.en: Why does a baby's cry make such an effective trap in these stories?

summary.id: Catatan 1589 menghubungkan patianac dengan perempuan dan anak yang mati saat melahirkan.
summary.en: The 1589 record links the patianac with a woman and child who died in childbirth.

summary.id: Orang Mandaya di Mindanao menyebutnya arwah anak yang ibunya meninggal sebelum melahirkan.
summary.en: The Mandaya of Mindanao call it the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth.

summary.id: Dalam versi Katolik ia arwah bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis, dan kini juga janin yang digugurkan.
summary.en: In the Catholic version it is the soul of an infant who died before baptism, and today also an aborted fetus.

Wikipedia, Aswang Project, dan Fansler tidak menjelaskan asal kata tiyanak, jadi dikosongkan.

short_description.id: Tiyanak adalah makhluk pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang menyamar sebagai bayi dan menangis di hutan untuk memikat pejalan, lalu kembali ke wujud aslinya dan menyerang.
short_description.en: The tiyanak is a vampiric creature of Philippine mythology that takes the form of a baby and cries in the jungle to lure travellers, then reverts to its true form and attacks.

long_description.id: Tiyanak, juga ditulis tianak atau tianac, adalah makhluk pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang berwujud balita atau bayi. Ia biasanya menjelma bayi baru lahir yang menangis di hutan untuk memikat pejalan; begitu diangkat, ia kembali ke wujud aslinya dan menyerang korbannya. Tiyanak juga digambarkan senang secara jahat menyesatkan pejalan atau menculik anak-anak, dan berbagai legenda sepakat bahwa ia mampu meniru bayi.
long_description.en: The tiyanak, also written tianak or tianac, is a vampiric being of Philippine mythology that appears as a toddler or baby. It usually appears as a newborn crying in the jungle to attract travellers; once picked up, it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim. It is also depicted as taking malevolent delight in leading travellers astray or abducting children, and different legends agree on its ability to mimic an infant.

long_description.id: Catatan tertulis tertua berasal dari Fr. Juan de Plasencia (1589), yang menulis tentang patianac: perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan dihukum bersama anaknya dan ratapannya terdengar pada malam hari. Uraian itu tidak menggambarkan bayi pemikat yang dikenal sekarang, dan ia menyatakan bahwa di antara semua orang Tagalog tidak ada lagi jejak kepercayaan semacam itu. Sebuah kumpulan cerita rakyat menjelaskan patianac sebagai roh kelahiran yang jahil, tinggal di hutan dan ladang, dan menyesatkan pejalan pada malam hari. Dalam catatan Cronicas karya Francisco de San Antonio (1738–44) dan Estadismo karya Martinez de Zuniga (1803), para pria menanggalkan pakaian dan, menurut yang terakhir, mengayunkan pedang agar patianac menjauh dari perempuan yang bersalin.
long_description.en: The oldest written record comes from Fr. Juan de Plasencia (1589), who wrote of the patianac: a woman who died in childbirth was punished together with her child and heard lamenting at night. That description does not present the familiar baby lure, and he states that among all the Tagalogs not a trace of such beliefs is left. A folklore collection explains the patianac as playful spirits of birth that dwell in woods and fields and mislead travellers by night. In San Antonio's Cronicas (1738–44) and Martinez de Zuniga's Estadismo (1803), men undress and, according to the latter, flourish a sword to keep the patianac away from a woman in labour.

long_description.id: Wujudnya berbeda menurut tempat. Dalam satu versi ia tetap berbentuk bayi tetapi menumbuhkan cakar dan taring tajam; dalam versi lain wujud sejatinya kakek kecil berkulit keriput, berjanggut dan berkumis panjang, berhidung pesek, dengan mata sebesar koin peseta. Di Pampanga tiyanak digambarkan sebagai orang kecil berkulit cokelat kacang yang melayang di udara; di pulau Mindoro ia berubah menjadi burung hitam; dan di Batangas ia digambarkan sebagai bayi biasa yang tersesat di alam liar. Menurut sebuah artikel tentang makhluk ini, rincian dari banyak tempat kadang tumpang tindih tetapi tidak membentuk satu anatomi baku. Dalam satu catatan, kakek kecil itu berkaki pincang, satu kakinya jauh lebih pendek, sehingga bergerak dengan lompatan mendadak.
long_description.en: Its form varies by place. In one version it keeps a baby's shape but grows sharp claws and fangs; in another its true form is a little old man with wrinkled skin, a long beard and moustache, a flat nose and eyes the size of peseta coins. In Pampanga the tiyanak appear as small people with nut-brown skin who hover instead of walking; on the island of Mindoro it turns into a black bird; and in Batangas it is described as regular babies lost in the wild. According to an article on the creature, details from many places sometimes overlap but do not form a single fixed anatomy. In one account the small old man had one leg much shorter than the other and moved in abrupt leaps.

long_description.id: Orang Mandaya di Mindanao memandang tiyanak sebagai arwah anak yang ibunya meninggal sebelum melahirkan; makhluk gaib serupa dalam cerita rakyat Melayu adalah pontianak. Dengan penjajahan Filipina oleh Spanyol pada abad ke-16, mitos tiyanak dipadukan dengan Katolik dan tiyanak dianggap arwah bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis; di Filipina masa kini pengertian itu meluas hingga mencakup janin yang digugurkan yang kembali untuk membalas dendam.
long_description.en: The Mandaya of Mindanao regard the tiyanak as the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth; the Pontianak of Malay folklore is a similar supernatural creature. Following the Spanish colonization of the Philippines in the 16th century, the myth became part of Catholicism and tiyanak came to be seen as the souls of infants who died before baptism; in modern-day Philippines the definition has extended to aborted fetuses that returned to seek revenge.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan setempat ada beberapa penangkal. Orang yang tersesat karena tangisan makhluk itu dipercaya dapat mematahkan pesonanya dengan membalik pakaian; suara keras seperti perayaan Tahun Baru dianggap mengusirnya; dan menurut Jose A. Samson, albularyo di pedesaan Luzon percaya bahwa memainkan gitar dapat menangkalnya. Dalam satu kisah, warga kampung memukul kaleng timah terus-menerus agar makhluk-makhluk itu melepaskan seorang penjaga kolam ikan yang hilang.
long_description.en: Local belief offers several countermeasures. Those led astray by the creature's cries are believed able to break the enchantment by turning their clothes inside out; loud noises such as a New Year's celebration are thought to drive it away; and according to Jose A. Samson, albularyos in rural Luzon believe that playing the guitar wards it off. In one story villagers struck tin cans continuously so that the beings would release a missing fishpond watchman.

claims.quote: is a vampiric creature in Philippine mythology that takes on the form of a toddler or baby. Although there are various types, it typically takes the form of a newborn baby and cries in the jungle to attract unwary travelers. Once it is picked up by an unfortunate passerby, it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim.

statement.id: Tiyanak adalah makhluk pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang berwujud balita atau bayi, biasanya bayi baru lahir yang menangis di hutan untuk memikat pejalan; begitu diangkat ia kembali ke wujud asli dan menyerang korbannya.
statement.en: The tiyanak is a vampiric creature of Philippine mythology in the form of a toddler or baby, usually a newborn crying in the jungle to attract travellers; once picked up it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim.

claims.quote: They had another deception—namely, that if any woman died in childbirth, she and the child suffered punishment; and that, at night, she could be heard lamenting. This was called patianac.

statement.id: Plasencia mencatat kepercayaan bahwa perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan dihukum bersama anaknya dan ratapannya terdengar di malam hari; ini disebut patianac.
statement.en: Plasencia recorded the belief that a woman who died in childbirth was punished with her child and heard lamenting at night; this was called patianac.

claims.quote: To counteract the malignity of this spirit, the husband, fastening the door, reduces himself to a state of complete nudity, lights a fire, and arming himself with his sword, continues to flourish it furiously, until the woman is delivered. ... Fr. Martinez de Zuniga, Estadismo (1803)

statement.id: Menurut Estadismo karya Martinez de Zuniga (1803), untuk melawan roh patianac sang suami mengunci pintu, menanggalkan seluruh pakaian, menyalakan api, dan mengayunkan pedang dengan garang sampai istrinya selesai bersalin.
statement.en: According to Martinez de Zuniga, Estadismo (1803), to counteract the patianac spirit the husband fastened the door, stripped completely naked, lit a fire and flourished his sword furiously until the woman was delivered.

claims.quote: In one version, it retains the general shape of a baby but then forms sharp claws and fangs to attack its victim.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi tiyanak tetap berbentuk umum seperti bayi tetapi menumbuhkan cakar dan taring tajam untuk menyerang korbannya.
statement.en: In one version the tiyanak retains the general shape of a baby but forms sharp claws and fangs to attack its victim.

claims.quote: In another version from Central Luzon, especially in Pampanga, the tiyanak are described as small, nut-brown people who don't walk on the ground but rather float on air.

statement.id: Dalam versi dari Luzon Tengah, terutama Pampanga, tiyanak digambarkan sebagai orang kecil berkulit cokelat kacang yang tidak berjalan di tanah melainkan melayang di udara.
statement.en: In a version from Central Luzon, especially Pampanga, the tiyanak are described as small, nut-brown people who do not walk on the ground but float on air.

claims.quote: The Mandaya people of Mindanao claim that the tiyanak is the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth.

statement.id: Orang Mandaya di Mindanao menyatakan bahwa tiyanak adalah arwah anak yang ibunya meninggal sebelum melahirkan.
statement.en: The Mandaya people of Mindanao claim that the tiyanak is the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth.

claims.quote: With the Spanish colonization of the Philippines in the 16th century, the tiyanak myth was integrated into Catholicism. The tiyanak in the Catholic version were supposedly the souls of infants that died before being baptized.

statement.id: Dengan penjajahan Filipina oleh Spanyol pada abad ke-16, mitos tiyanak dipadukan dengan Katolik; dalam versi Katolik tiyanak dianggap arwah bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis.
statement.en: With the Spanish colonization of the Philippines in the 16th century the tiyanak myth was integrated into Catholicism; in the Catholic version tiyanak were supposedly the souls of infants who died before being baptized.

claims.quote: Those that were led astray by the creature's cries are believed to be able to break the enchantment by turning their clothes inside out.

statement.id: Orang yang tersesat karena tangisan makhluk itu dipercaya dapat mematahkan pesonanya dengan membalik pakaian mereka.
statement.en: Those led astray by the creature’s cries are believed able to break the enchantment by turning their clothes inside out.

statement.id: Catatan tentang patianac berasal dari Fr. Juan de Plasencia tentang orang Tagalog (1589).
statement.en: The patianac account is from Fr. Juan de Plasencia on the Tagalogs (1589).

claims.quote: The tiyanak (also tianak or tianac ... is a vampiric creature in Philippine mythology that takes on the form of a toddler or baby.

statement.en: The tiyanak is also written tianak or tianac.

statement.en: The tiyanak is also depicted as taking malevolent delight in leading travellers astray or abducting children.

statement.id: Berbagai legenda sepakat bahwa tiyanak mampu meniru bayi, termasuk meniru tangisan bayi untuk memikat korban.
statement.en: The stories agree on the tiyanak's ability to mimic an infant, including imitating an infant's cries to lure victims.

claims.quote: In this version, the "true" form of the tiyanak is that of a little old man with wrinkled skin, a long beard and mustache, a flat nose and eyes the size of peseta coins.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi, wujud "sejati" tiyanak adalah kakek kecil berkulit keriput, berjanggut dan berkumis panjang, berhidung pesek, dengan mata sebesar koin peseta.
statement.en: In one version the "true" form of the tiyanak is a little old man with wrinkled skin, a long beard and moustache, a flat nose and eyes the size of peseta coins.

claims.quote: In yet another story it is seen supernaturally flying through the forest (still in the form of a baby) and in a legend from the island of Mindoro it transforms into a black bird before flying away

statement.id: Dalam cerita lain tiyanak terlihat terbang secara gaib di hutan (masih berwujud bayi), dan dalam legenda dari pulau Mindoro ia berubah menjadi burung hitam sebelum terbang pergi.
statement.en: In another story the tiyanak is seen supernaturally flying through the forest (still in the form of a baby), and in a legend from the island of Mindoro it turns into a black bird before flying away.

claims.quote: In the Batangas version, the tiyanak are described as regular babies who were lost in the wild.

statement.en: A similar supernatural creature in Malay folklore is the Pontianak, which was a woman who died before giving birth.

claims.quote: In modern-day Philippines, this definition has extended to that of aborted fetuses that returned from death to seek revenge on those who deprived them of life.

statement.id: Di Filipina masa kini, pengertian ini meluas hingga mencakup janin yang digugurkan yang kembali dari kematian untuk membalas dendam kepada mereka yang merenggut hidupnya.
statement.en: In modern-day Philippines this definition has extended to aborted fetuses that returned from death to take revenge on those who deprived them of life.

claims.quote: Loud noises such as a New Year's celebration are also thought to be enough to drive the tiyanak away from the vicinity.

statement.id: Suara keras seperti perayaan Tahun Baru juga dianggap cukup untuk mengusir tiyanak dari sekitar.
statement.en: Loud noises such as a New Year's celebration are also thought to be enough to drive the tiyanak away from the vicinity.

claims.quote: According to Jose A. Samson, a common belief among albularyos in rural Luzon in how to ward off the tiyanak is to play the guitar

statement.id: Menurut Jose A. Samson, kepercayaan umum di kalangan albularyo (tabib tradisional) di pedesaan Luzon untuk menangkal tiyanak adalah memainkan gitar.
statement.en: According to Jose A. Samson, a common belief among albularyos in rural Luzon for warding off the tiyanak is to play the guitar.

claims.quote: The tiyanak is the subject of many Philippine films: Tianak (1953) Tiyanak (1988)

statement.id: Tiyanak menjadi subjek banyak film Filipina, di antaranya Tianak (1953) dan Tiyanak (1988).
statement.en: The tiyanak is the subject of many Philippine films, among them Tianak (1953) and Tiyanak (1988).

claims.quote: May the honor and glory be God our Lord's, that among all the Tagalos not a trace of this is left

statement.id: Setelah mencatat patianac, sumber itu menyatakan bahwa di antara semua orang Tagalog tidak ada lagi jejak kepercayaan ini.
statement.en: After recording the patianac, the source states that among all the Tagalogs not a trace of this is left.

claims.quote: When a woman is about to give birth, some men undress until they are stark naked. ... They say that it is to keep the patiànac and the osuàng away from the woman. These are witches among them who come to obstruct the success of the childbirth, and to suck out the souls of children ... Fr. Francisco de San Antonio, Cronicas (1738–44)

statement.id: Menurut Cronicas karya Francisco de San Antonio (1738–44), ketika seorang perempuan hendak melahirkan, sejumlah pria menanggalkan pakaian; mereka mengatakan itu untuk menjauhkan patianac dan osuang, penyihir yang datang menghalangi kelancaran persalinan dan menyedot jiwa anak-anak.
statement.en: According to Cronicas by Francisco de San Antonio (1738–44), when a woman is about to give birth some men undress completely; they say this is to keep the patianac and the osuang away, witches who come to obstruct the childbirth and suck out the souls of children.

claims.quote: In 1589, the Franciscan missionary Juan de Plasencia included the patianac among beings feared by Tagalog communities. His short description does not present the familiar monster disguised as an abandoned baby. Instead, it concerns a woman and child who die during childbirth and are said to be heard lamenting at night.
claims.locator: A Belief with More Than One History

statement.id: Pada 1589 misionaris Fransiskan Juan de Plasencia memasukkan patianac di antara makhluk yang ditakuti komunitas Tagalog. Uraiannya tidak menggambarkan monster bayi terlantar yang dikenal sekarang, melainkan seorang perempuan dan anaknya yang mati saat melahirkan dan konon terdengar meratap pada malam hari.
statement.en: In 1589 the Franciscan missionary Juan de Plasencia included the patianac among beings feared by Tagalog communities. His description does not present the familiar monster disguised as an abandoned baby but concerns a woman and child who die in childbirth and are said to be heard lamenting at night.

claims.quote: Accounts from Malolos, Malabon, Batangas, Mindoro, Pampanga, and other places describe deceptive crying, altered sight, lost time, a child on a banana leaf, uneven legs, claws, or a sudden transformation. These details sometimes overlap, but they do not form a single fixed anatomy.

statement.id: Catatan dari Malolos, Malabon, Batangas, Mindoro, Pampanga, dan tempat lain menggambarkan tangisan yang menipu, penglihatan yang berubah, waktu yang hilang, anak di atas daun pisang, kaki tak sama panjang, cakar, atau perubahan mendadak. Rincian itu kadang tumpang tindih tetapi tidak membentuk satu anatomi baku.
statement.en: Accounts from Malolos, Malabon, Batangas, Mindoro, Pampanga and other places describe deceptive crying, altered sight, lost time, a child on a banana leaf, uneven legs, claws or a sudden transformation. These details sometimes overlap but do not form a single fixed anatomy.

claims.quote: two boys found what appeared to be a naked, unusually plump newborn lying on the side of a banana leaf. ... The child changed while they fondled it. The round infant body became that of a small old man.
claims.locator: The Infant on the Banana Leaf

statement.id: Dalam satu catatan, dua anak lelaki menemukan sesuatu yang tampak seperti bayi baru lahir yang telanjang dan montok di atas daun pisang; saat mereka mengelusnya, tubuh bulat bayi itu berubah menjadi tubuh seorang kakek kecil.
statement.en: In one account two boys found what appeared to be a naked, unusually plump newborn lying on a banana leaf; while they fondled it the round infant body became that of a small old man.

claims.quote: One leg was much shorter than the other, so the being could not move with an ordinary human stride. It travelled in abrupt leaps.
claims.locator: The Infant on the Banana Leaf

statement.id: Dalam catatan yang sama, satu kaki makhluk itu jauh lebih pendek daripada yang lain sehingga ia tidak dapat melangkah seperti manusia biasa dan bergerak dengan lompatan mendadak.
statement.en: In the same account one leg of the being was much shorter than the other, so it could not move with an ordinary human stride and travelled in abrupt leaps.

claims.quote: People in the barrio suspected that the tianak had taken him. They did not search quietly. The party carried tin cans and struck them continuously, hoping that a tremendous racket would frighten the beings and force them to release their victim.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, warga kampung menduga tianak telah membawa seorang penjaga kolam ikan yang tua; rombongan pencari memukul kaleng timah terus-menerus dengan harapan kegaduhan itu menakuti makhluk-makhluk tersebut dan memaksa mereka melepaskan korbannya.
statement.en: In one story villagers of a barrio suspected that the tianak had taken an elderly fishpond watchman; the search party struck tin cans continuously, hoping the racket would frighten the beings and force them to release their victim.

claims.quote: The Tianak — Tagalog ... The wife held it to her breast even though she had not yet borne a child and had no milk to give. The infant fastened onto her. A moment later she cried out that it had bitten her. ... She was dead. The infant was no longer beside her. Looking into the forest, he saw it flying away among the trees.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Tagalog tentang sepasang suami istri, bayi yang mereka temukan di hutan menempel pada dada sang istri dan menggigitnya; sang istri kemudian ditemukan mati, dan suaminya melihat bayi itu terbang pergi di antara pepohonan.
statement.en: In a Tagalog tale of a young couple, the infant they found in the forest fastened onto the wife’s breast and bit her; she was later found dead and her husband saw the infant flying away among the trees.

claims.quote: The Patianak — Tagalog, Oriental Mindoro ... The baby would not stop feeding. It remained fixed at her breast while her strength drained away. She became weaker and weaker until she died. Once she was dead, the infant changed into a black bird and flew from the house.

statement.id: Dalam kisah patianak dari Mindoro Oriental, bayi yang disusui seorang ibu tidak berhenti menyusu sementara tenaga sang ibu terkuras sampai ia meninggal; setelah itu bayi tersebut berubah menjadi burung hitam dan terbang dari rumah.
statement.en: In the patianak story from Oriental Mindoro, the baby a mother nursed would not stop feeding while her strength drained until she died; the infant then changed into a black bird and flew from the house.

claims.quote: Bata and the Tianac — Tagalog ... The story closes by explaining the Tianac as a child who died without baptism. Such beings were said to wander lonely places, become visible or invisible, and mislead young people. Turning one’s clothing inside out was given as a way to break their power of deception.

statement.id: Kisah Tagalog tentang Bata menjelaskan tianac sebagai anak yang meninggal tanpa dibaptis; makhluk semacam itu dikatakan berkeliaran di tempat sunyi, dapat menampakkan diri atau tidak terlihat, dan menyesatkan anak muda. Membalik pakaian disebut sebagai cara mematahkan daya tipunya.
statement.en: The Tagalog story of Bata explains the Tianac as a child who died without baptism; such beings were said to wander lonely places, become visible or invisible and mislead young people, and turning one’s clothing inside out was given as a way to break their power of deception.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... Small beings appeared around him. They were nut-brown and some floated in the air. They had large noses, wide mouths, and fierce eyes.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Dalam kisah Kapampangan, makhluk-makhluk kecil berkulit cokelat kacang muncul mengelilingi seorang lelaki; sebagian melayang di udara, berhidung besar, bermulut lebar, dan bermata garang.
statement.en: In the Kapampangan story small nut-brown beings appeared around a man; some floated in the air and they had large noses, wide mouths and fierce eyes.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... An elderly servant told the narrator that Vicente had once encountered many tianac on Mount Arayat.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Menurut kisah Kapampangan, seorang lelaki bernama Vicente pernah bertemu banyak tianac di Gunung Arayat.
statement.en: In the Kapampangan story, a man named Vicente once encountered many tianac on Mount Arayat.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... He removed his clothes, turned them inside out, and put them on again. The crowd vanished immediately.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, sang lelaki melepas pakaiannya, membaliknya, lalu memakainya lagi, dan kerumunan makhluk itu langsung lenyap.
statement.en: In the story the man removed his clothes, turned them inside out and put them on again, and the crowd vanished immediately.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... Only then did he learn that it was Monday. Vicente had entered the mountain on Saturday and believed that he was merely an hour late for the meeting.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang sama, Vicente baru mengetahui bahwa hari sudah Senin; ia masuk gunung pada hari Sabtu dan mengira hanya terlambat satu jam dari pertemuan.
statement.en: In the same story Vicente learned only afterwards that it was Monday; he had entered the mountain on Saturday and believed he was merely an hour late for the meeting.

claims.quote: Muntianak — a related name reported in parts of the southern Philippines; it should not be assumed to share every Tagalog detail.

statement.id: Muntianak adalah nama terkait yang dilaporkan di beberapa bagian Filipina selatan; tidak boleh diasumsikan memiliki semua rincian versi Tagalog.
statement.en: Muntianak is a related name reported in parts of the southern Philippines; it should not be assumed to share every Tagalog detail.

claims.quote: Pregnancy and labour could be dangerous, infant mortality was common, and an unexplained cry outside the settlement demanded a moral response. The listener is placed in an impossible position: ignoring a child would be cruel, but answering the cry may expose the rescuer to danger.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, kehamilan dan persalinan bisa berbahaya, kematian bayi lazim, dan tangisan tak dikenal di luar permukiman menuntut tanggapan moral; pendengar berada dalam posisi yang mustahil: mengabaikan anak itu kejam, tetapi menjawab tangisannya dapat membahayakan penolong.
statement.en: According to the article, pregnancy and labour could be dangerous, infant mortality was common and an unexplained cry outside the settlement demanded a moral response; the listener is placed in an impossible position, since ignoring a child would be cruel but answering the cry may expose the rescuer to danger.

claims.quote: Modern writers and artists continue to reinterpret the Tiyanak. ... Acuña proposes that the Tiyanak can be read as more than a mindless killer: the figure may also be approached as a newborn trying to understand a violent world created by adults.

statement.id: Penulis dan seniman modern terus menafsirkan ulang tiyanak; Acuña mengusulkan bahwa tiyanak dapat dibaca sebagai lebih dari pembunuh tanpa pikiran, yaitu bayi yang berusaha memahami dunia kejam ciptaan orang dewasa.
statement.en: Modern writers and artists continue to reinterpret the tiyanak; Acuña proposes that the tiyanak can be read as more than a mindless killer, as a newborn trying to understand a violent world created by adults.

claims.quote: a cry resembling that of an abandoned infant draws a traveller toward the roadside, forest, field, or swamp, where the helpless child proves to be something dangerous.

statement.id: Tangisan menyerupai bayi terlantar memikat pejalan menuju tepi jalan, hutan, ladang, atau rawa, tempat anak yang tak berdaya itu ternyata berbahaya.
statement.en: A cry resembling that of an abandoned infant draws a traveller toward the roadside, forest, field or swamp, where the helpless child proves to be something dangerous.

claims.quote: Patianac, mischievous birth-spirits that live in the woods and fields, and lead travellers astray at night.

statement.id: Catatan kaki dalam kumpulan cerita itu menjelaskan patianac sebagai roh kelahiran yang jahil, tinggal di hutan dan ladang, dan menyesatkan pejalan pada malam hari.
statement.en: A footnote in the story collection explains patianac as mischievous birth-spirits that live in the woods and fields and lead travellers astray at night.
